_patch_meta.description: Insert 2 draft glossary entries for the surface relation terms (escalation #2548). Section type glossary_programme already exists.

record.heading: surface relation
record.body:
[DEFINITION] A link between two surfaces that an outside source, WordNet 3.0, gives: they share a sense (synonym), are opposed (antonym), are derived forms of one another (derivational), stand in similar adjective senses (similar) or resolve to one WordNet base form (same_base). Each pair is held once, with a weight that counts the links.

[BACKGROUND] Held in surface_relation, one row per pair of the single-word surfaces of the relation study; the scope and the rule for type and weight are settings (surfaces.relation_scope, surfaces.relation_pair_rules). WordNet is modern general English, so a relation is a candidate to read, not a finding of the study, and nothing it gives is written to a base. It is a second view beside the collections, not a replacement for them (escalation #2548).
record.author: claude_code

record.heading: network group
record.body:
[DEFINITION] A set of surfaces joined by surface relations, directly or through other surfaces. The largest group joins most of the surfaces into one connected mass; the smaller groups (two to fifteen surfaces) are sets of surfaces that WordNet draws together; a surface with no relation to any other is a group of one.

[BACKGROUND] Held in surface_network_group, one row per surface per grouping, kind main, small or no_pair; the earlier grouping is kept when a new one is made. The researcher takes the small groups as clear concepts and deals by hand with the surfaces that have no pair; these are the researcher's readings, recorded as such (escalations #2545, #2548).
